The Citizens' Committee and the Hungry Masses

[Zagłębie — relief and unemployment; opinion piece.] (Support for the unemployed and the ignoring of the hungry. — The tasks of the Jewish members.)
We in Zagłębie have citizens' committees for the unemployed, whose aim and task is to help the working masses who are not earning. That the situation of the working element is a hard one, that they go hungry together with their wives and children — there are no two opinions about it. Every one of us knows how hard it is for them to get through a day, and with what self-sacrifice they keep up their existence. The citizens' committees in Zagłębie therefore have a very sacred and responsible mission in supplying basic necessities of life to these hungry masses, whose number, unfortunately, grows with such giant strides from day to day.
That is one side of the medal. But there is also a second side, on which one must also dwell. True, the workers who have no employment are hungry — but are they alone hungry, and is it only they who must be helped out of grave want? Are there so few hungry people besides them? Are there so few unemployed who are not professional workers? The committees give support to the people registered at the municipal offices (magistrates) as unemployed; but what are the great masses of people to do, who have nothing to do and cannot be registered at the municipal offices as unemployed? What are the craftsmen to do, who have been hungry for a long, long time and no longer even remember what a stitch of work looks like? What are the impoverished artisans to do, who for months on end have not gone near their workshops and go hungry together with their wives and children, just like the hungry workers? What are the pedlars to do, who used to make an honourable living hauling their bundles on their shoulders through the villages? What are those elements to do who for a long time have not been able to afford even a trade licence (patent) and languish hungry in their lonely little rooms? Does this great mass of people not deserve to be supported just as well as the wretched worker? Must one not grant this mass the same trust as the unemployed man? Are they not called unemployed? Are they not in need of help[?] to exactly the same extent?
True, certain quantities of products have been allotted to them too, but it is like a bone tossed out, as if it were something superfluous, as if one were doing somebody a favour; moreover, the quantity tossed out is a minimum which falls far short of satisfying this hungry mass.
Do we not have the right to demand that the impoverished elements, too, should benefit from the support in proportion? Are we to blame that the gates of the factories are closed to us and we cannot be classified as workers? There is, after all, a rule that hunger does not distinguish which category it belongs to. Each of us has the same stomach, and every body is made of human material; so that once it is a matter of supporting the hungry with food, no distinction can be made, and it must not be allowed to lead to such a practice[?].
And besides — why should we not claim our rights, [rights] which are due to us, and [concerning] campaigns to which we relate with full seriousness and which we support as is proper, quite often beyond our strength? The money is taken from the town's householders, from the merchants, from local events (imprezy) and from the municipal budgets; it seems that our capital is represented everywhere, and it has always been known that in giving we are the first — merciful sons of the merciful are we — let alone when it is a matter of giving alms to the hungry for bread: everywhere we are the first and occupy a very honourable place. So we have the right to demand that our hungry, too, be supported when they have no possibility of registering as unemployed.
We live, after all, in a terrible time; it is simply impossible to grasp with the mind how we drag the yoke of existence upon ourselves — so how can one, in such a hard time, distinguish one hungry person from another hungry person? Does not every hungry person live to the same degree?
Yes, we support the committees; we carry the burdens of the institutions together with everyone else, if not more; so that already from this standpoint we have the right to demand that our hungry not be ignored and slighted — they who suffer together with everyone from the grave crisis that has spread itself broad and firm upon our shoulders.
In the present hard time, at such a catastrophic moment, one must not distinguish and classify who is a registered unemployed person and who is not. Under today's conditions the tactic, the system in general, must be changed: we must carry out the campaigns under the slogan of supporting the hungry. The citizens' committee for supporting, therefore [sic: "alzo"], the unemployed must support all those who are hungry, all those who have nothing with which to get through the day. That is the turn that must be taken; that is the motto[?] under which the useful activity must be conducted. Bread and potatoes must be given in the same proportion to all who are hungry, all who have nothing to put into their mouths.
Earlier, when the situation was not so sad, when conditions were still normal, when the middle class was not yet so broken and ruined, we looked away. At that time we took care separately of our sufferers, not considering that they needed to be supported by the general local committees, which were supported by us in proper measure. We knew perfectly well that in giving we must be the first — and not only the first, but that we must give twofold: once for sufferers in general, among whom, of course, Jews are also counted, and a second time we ourselves must take care of our Jewish sufferers, who in those circles were either not provided for, or the provision was such that with what we gave over and above it[?] we were far from discharging our duty; so that, wishing to do our duty by ourselves as well, we had to carry out separate campaigns specially for Jewish sufferers, Jewish hungry.
We did not balk at the double burden which, in truth, we dragged with difficulty on our shoulders, regardless of the fact that the load was superfluous and irrational. Just as we would not balk at it now either — but the trouble is that nowadays the Jewish community is exhausted: the broad strata of our population, those who are the givers, those who mostly give beyond their means — they are ruined and almost fallen below the normal line, so that even with the best will we cannot play the double financial role.
The committees, into which Jewish money also flows, must absolutely also take care of the Jewish hungry — of those who are broken and languish in the darkness, waiting to be provided with a piece of bread and a korzec [a dry measure] of coal.
Even with the best will, we are not now in a position to carry out separate campaigns for our hungry.
Since there are Jewish representatives sitting on the committees, they must react to all this. They must not allow our hungry to be wronged and ignored; they must stand on guard and protect as is proper the interests of our oppressed, who have come to such a state that they yearn to receive from the town a free potato for themselves and a piece of bread for their little children. It is enough for us that hungry people come begging to be given something to put in their mouths.
We are sure that if we are not treated like stepchildren, if our hungry are not for the committees like a superfluous burden one wants to be rid of and supports only for form's sake — then the middle class will be able[?] to cope with it, and all those who still have the means to give will certainly increase their commitment to supporting the existing committees.
Our representatives who sit there must exert pressure on their colleagues, so that our hungry are supported on an equal footing with the Christian unemployed. They must prove to them that we are represented there in an honourable way with the finances, and therefore we also have the right to demand that in the distribution of the products, too, we occupy the same place.
One would like to hope, we want to believe, that with proper elucidation of the question, with proper presentation of the matter, people will after all understand that our demands are rational and that our claims must be fulfilled.
The main thing is to stand on guard and to defend our interests, in which the Jewish masses have a vital — a bloody — stake.
That is what is important. That is how we must see to it that the position is not neglected.
R. Let[?].
It's Hard to Be Great...

[Satirical feuilleton — power and rulers.]
Pini Baal-Lashon.
I met one of my boyhood friends, whom I had not seen for many years.
In our boyhood years we were companions from the same beit-midrash, both of us toiling in the "tent of Torah." Afterwards both of us set out into the wide world.
And in the wide world our paths parted.
I went on along the path of "books and writings." A poor path and a quiet one. And he went off along the path of "money and riches." A glittering path and a noisy one.
And after a span of years we met by chance, and my friend began complaining to me about his life.
"What? You're complaining?" I asked him. "Why, you're somebody great and rich, and you crack [?] the long whip!"
And he leaned towards me in a friendly way and said:
"Oh, good brother, if only I could be what I once was — then I would know what living is! Look here, I'm rich and great now, and I don't have a hundredth of the pleasure I had from life when I was poor. Once upon a time, when my wife set before me at midday a plate of potatoes with bread, and I knew I had earned it the hard way, I tasted all sorts of flavours in that dish, it was sweet as sugar, and I hoped that if I could eat a cutlet, no one would be my equal!... And today, when they set the finest dishes before me at the table — there's no pleasure in it! My head is torn into hundreds of pieces, my businesses give me no rest, don't let me sleep; I'm only afraid that I might slip and become a poor man again."
It's hard to be great, my friend! Because the fear of becoming small again drives a person mad!...
———
An ordinary meeting, an ordinary thing — yet it led me to another thought. About the small ones who have become great in our time.
About the oppressed who have seized power into their own hands.
In our days many "under-beadles" have become head "beadles."
Many of the oppressed have seized power into their hands and become great.
And once you become great, you don't want to become small again. And once you come to power, you don't want to lose it. And when you don't want to lose it, you forget everything you yourself preached before. And when you forget, you use all sorts of means to hold on to power, and when you use all sorts of means, you no longer choose between kosher and non-kosher, honest and forbidden. And when you no longer choose, you don't want to hear or remember even for what purpose you came to power in the first place...
Take Russia, for example.
With how many slogans of freedom the "Red liberators" came! They preached that every state must conduct open diplomacy, without secrets from the world; secrets, they said, are a lie, a sin against the people; the people must know everything the state intends to do.
And ever since they have been in power, the "people" walks about in the dark and has not even an inkling. And diplomacy is always a secret of secrets.
They argued that no one must be made into an "idol": dead — buried, the earth has covered him, it's over with him. Only a name remains. Not to mention spending a penny of the people's money on him — that is forbidden.
And they themselves did with their Lenin what was once done with the Pharaohs in Egypt: embalmed him and kept him in a glass case, so that the people should come to bow down to him.
And who can even count the things the liberators promised before, and on coming to power did the very opposite?
Or, for example, Mussolini, the former socialist.
In what iron gloves he has taken hold of his country and holds it, so that no one can draw a free breath!
And here we come, indeed, to the English socialists, with the deeds they inflict on us Jews most harshly of all.
When MacDonald and Webb were still under-beadles and were looking out for the happy moment when they would become the "head beadles" of England, they were our best friends.
Before, when MacDonald made a journey to the Land of Israel and saw what the halutzim had accomplished, he sang himself hoarse with praises for us and told the whole world about the good fortune awaiting the Arabs and the whole world from the Jewish homeland in Eretz-Israel.
He was angry at the previous government, which put out against us every Monday and Thursday "White Papers" with restrictions.
And now, when he himself has settled into the soft chair of government, he has played on a worse pipe than the old bourgeois government did, and has made for us almost "a weeping for generations" — may we yet one day be able to tell of it in joy.
———
And listen: we are, heaven forbid, no enemies of India, but we are very much afraid that even if the saintly Gandhi came to power, he too could not withstand the test and would become other than what he is now.
Who knows? After all, we see that power turns the mind, poisons and spoils the most decent people in the world.
And it may well be that if one were quietly, secretly, to ask all these power-holders who have grown great, whispering in their ear, they too might perhaps complain, like that friend of mine, that they had more pleasure from life when they were "small."
But that's how it is. Nobody wants to go back.
Yes, it's hard to be great. Because precisely this fear of becoming "small" again drives one mad.
And that is precisely why mad politics rules in our days.
And not for nothing did a Jewish sage of ours, Rabbi Shlomo ibn Gabirol, say:
"He who wishes to defeat evil with yet greater evil, in order to hold on to power, is himself defeated!..."
A pity, listen, that the power-holders don't study our musar books — they would become far more decent, upon my life.
"That They Defile Not Their Camps..."

[Editorial — informing and informers; Będzin/Zagłębie.] In today's struggle against informing and informers!

Informing, informers — everyone thinks about it, everyone knows that this worm has dug itself firmly into the social organism and is laying waste to the individual as well as the community, demoralising every corner, desecrating all that is holy — and on top of that expects to be thanked nicely for it.

Informers. One meets them, one shakes their hand, one even treats them with the greatest respect. At first it is said that one does so out of fear, but little by little the informer will become the "most exemplary" citizen; others, and he himself, will begin to think and believe that informing is in fact the finest virtue, and the informer — the noblest of men.

This plague is, alas, no longer "not upon us" in Zagłębie either. And therefore we warmly welcome the stand taken by the Jewish Merchants' Association in Siedlce, which publishes the names of the informers in the local newspaper there.

———

It is not enough that the Jewish merchant is weighed down by the crisis, taxes, municipal levies, various sanitary and administrative regulations, poor takings, lack of credit and sharpened competition — all of which break him and ruin his existence — lately an even greater plague has been added, one that surpasses them all: I N F O R M I N G. Insofar as[?] the first troubles and difficulties are to a certain extent a common misfortune striking the whole merchant class, the last misfortune is almost specifically Jewish. Among our neighbours the ugly phenomenon of one merchant informing on another is not to be seen.

To our great shame, informing has become an everyday phenomenon among us. One merchant informs on another, the worker on the employer, the journeyman on the master, the employee on the business owner; people inform for revenge, to trip someone up, for the sake of competition — and there is no lack of plain informers either, informers by profession.

The tax regulations are harsh, the administrative ordinances almost unbearable, the tax and administrative authorities are strict — yet there are moments when a certain deviation from the harsh law is overlooked, when conforming to the letter of the law has become impossible or unbearable under the difficult conditions.

The merchants' organisations, which are in frequent contact with the competent spheres and mediate between those who execute and those who guard the law, often find possibilities to moderate and regulate the strict demands — if not for the community as a whole, then at any rate for impoverished, hounded, half- or fully ruined individuals. Such achievements, concessions and mitigations of the law would often have come about — were it not for the I N F O R M E R S. These pests often penetrate precisely into the narrowed places of goodwill that would have been attained, and cause the destruction of those who have fallen.

True, the competent spheres regard them, the informers, to some degree with disgust, with the greatest contempt, but at the same time with fear for their own existence: they, the informers, strike fear into some of the representatives of authority. There is no lack even of explicit threats to file complaints with the central authorities against the lenient guardians of the law for alleged neglect of their duties.

The matter must not remain thus; it is already beginning to become a system; respected merchants already permit themselves to use this system, even people who lay claim to public honours.

We appeal to Jewish society and demand moral support; we call on all societies, associations, houses of prayer, minyanim and similar institutions to apply the "and they shall put out of the camp" to all these plagues and blights that have grown up among us.

We firmly believe in the power of society to carry the struggle through, so that those who have gone astray will think better of it and part with their ugly deeds; the social boycott will also deter and restrain others from corrupt acts.

We make the sad beginning in today's issue of the paper: we publish the first person whom we have established to have committed the offence of informing against competitors. We will not refrain from publishing further names if this bacchanalia does not stop.

We approach this cleansing[?] with the greatest sense of responsibility, even at the cost of legal consequences. This must come to an end — "that they defile not their camps."

———

It would be useful and just if the beginning made in Siedlce were continued in Zagłębie.
"And they shall put out of the camp"
"That they defile not their camps"
These commands are now the order of the hour!
Y. N-m.
The Tasks of the Maccabi World Union

A conversation with Dr. A. Rosenfeld.

For several days the vice-president of the Maccabi World Union, Dr. Alexander Rosenfeld, stayed in Zagłębie, and in a conversation with the writer of these lines he said the following:

— The main task of my present journey through Poland is to bring clarity into the ranks of the Jewish sportsmen. Until now the Jewish sports clubs did not clearly know the true aims of "Maccabi". True, the athletes instinctively felt an interest in national achievements and took part in national appearances, but still there was no clarity in the work. Maccabi's present task is to make clear that by belonging to "Maccabi" one places oneself in the service of the national ideal.

That is the face of "Maccabi" in other countries, more or less; only in Poland has the idea not yet crystallized. This is also important for the sports society "Hakoach" in Będzin, which is likewise affiliated to the Maccabi World Union. Incidentally, the last Maccabiah in Eretz Israel showed the world what "Maccabi" strives for. The same aspiration, however, must exist in all Jewish sports clubs.

— The purpose of your visit?

— My task is to propagate and carry out the campaign for the lofty idea of "Kfar HaMaccabi", the first Jewish sports colony in Eretz Israel.

"Kfar HaMaccabi" is to become the centre of Jewish sport in the whole world. A model Jewish school of physical culture will be created there, a central camp for training instructors for Jewish sport, and also to raise and develop Jewish sport in Eretz Israel, so that in time it can represent the Jewish people in the international sports arena.

— The funds?

— All Jewish sports clubs will have to collect the necessary fund. The work for this goal will be a great undertaking of "Maccabi", because its members are obliged to perform national deeds — to help redeem land that is bound up with memories of the most beautiful heroic era of the Jewish people.

— The Winter Maccabiah in Zakopane.

— In the first days of February of the year 1933 a Jewish sports festival will take place in Zakopane. The meaning of the Winter Maccabiah is first of all to show the European world that winter sport is already developed among Jews too. A large part of the Jewish people also understands the beauty of nature, and to escape for a while from the city with its troubles to the mountains, to unite with free nature.

At the Winter Maccabiah in Zakopane, which will have the character of a popular sport event, thousands of Jewish winter athletes from Czechoslovakia, Germany, Austria and Romania will meet — besides the 2000 young people from Czechoslovakia, who are very good winter sportsmen.

The Polish sports authorities show a special interest in the Winter Maccabiah in Zakopane. In every town, in Zagłębie too, I see the great preparations for the sports event.

— The further task of the World Union?

— On Maccabi's agenda now stand the following tasks: 1) the second Maccabiah in Eretz Israel in the year 1935, which will be much better organized than the first. Jewish athletes from very distant communities, which the news that a Maccabiah takes place in Eretz Israel did not reach at all, will also take part in it; 2) to prepare the Jewish participation in the international women's sports games in London in the year 1934. For the first time in Jewish history the Jewish flag will wave in the international arena; and 3) to organize the Maccabiah that will take place in August 1933 in Czernowitz.

At the end of our conversation the honoured guest asked me to convey in his name a hearty "yishar koach" to the music section of the Będzin "Hakoach".

Sh. L-ch.
Without Sanctities

[Essay — thought and culture.] By Leo Koenig.
The Soviet press has become angry with its own Commissar of Justice, Krylenko, because he used the word “holy” in one of his latest decrees.
And do you think he used the word in reference to one of the old bourgeois sanctities? — God forbid; in today’s Russia that would have been a sin over which one does not just get a little angry and make up right away. He did not use the word “holy” in connection with any religion, nor even in connection with any art.
With the word “holy” he designated the property that belongs to the collective, to the whole of present-day Soviet society: “The property of the proletariat is holy, and all those who steal from the collective will from today onward be punished most severely.”
And yet people got angry with him for having used the word “holy” even in reference to the goods of the commune.
It seems to me that this tiny fact is more than characteristic of our time. It is almost symbolic: not only have many sanctities already been destroyed for a large part of present-day humanity, but this very process of destruction has only just begun!..
And what is even more important: not only in today’s Russia, but even in the countries where all our inherited official and unofficial sanctities still reign, the naive and deep faith in them has already been badly undermined...
People still speak automatically of sanctities, still serve them atavistically, but the rational spirit, which penetrates ever further into all strata and corners of present-day life, has already destroyed the naivety, the true and simple faith in sanctities.
In the countries and in the strata that claim to be our avant-garde, the bearers of a better future, people are already ashamed even of the word “holy”, even when it is applied to genuinely positive and rational phenomena.
Why deny it: the word “holy” has already become unfit in the language of modern people. What modern person still dares consciously to use that word?
True, the word still slips out (even from a Soviet commissar), and no wonder: for thousands of years people have used the word; for thousands of years people have created and served false and true sanctities.
It is therefore natural that the word and the concept should go on being used for a long time. But consciously, today’s rational person is already ashamed to use the word.
What modern writer or artist will not be ashamed to use the words “holy art”, for example, which were used so often only yesterday?
What present-day man of science will speak of “holy science”?
What idealist or revolutionary will dare to speak even of the “holy ideals” for which so many sacrifices were once made?
A socialist who speaks today of his holy ideal risks being counted among the “lower middle class”, to which belong such sentimentalists as George Lansbury and even Maxton.
A person who speaks of sanctities is treated today with the greatest suspicion[?] — even if he uses them in connection with the most revolutionary ideas and ideals.
Common sense, iron laws, scientific approaches, tangible interests... facts, facts and facts once again. That is what the modern spirit of the age demands — but not sanctities.
— — —
But far more symptomatic is not that sanctities are now out of fashion, but that at bottom even those who keep talking about them no longer believe in them.
What is holy today? Human life? Private property? The suffering of the insulted and oppressed? Children’s tears? Ideals? Or the religions and their sects, which keep tearing at one another and competing to the point of bloodshed? These are today no longer sanctities but “empty phrases”.
Everything nowadays is measured and weighed on the scales of interests; everything else is sentimentalism, hypocrisy, which are themselves exploited under the dictatorship of interests.
Nowadays there are no sanctities — at least not in the great public domain in which we live.
Perhaps a holy eternal lamp still glows warm in the hearts of a few individuals, but outside it is cold, an ice-cold frost of hard interests and bitter struggle.
Love, sanctities — the modern, rationalistic and scientific spirit of the age has extinguished them, is in the process of extinguishing them...
And it becomes cold and frosty to live without heart and with bitter struggle, [with nothing] to warm one a little.
— — —
Lament the sanctities already destroyed and the sanctities about to be destroyed?
There are enough people who do so and will go on doing so. Jerubbaals[?], who wail like hungry jackals over the holy ruins, and sincere Jeremiahs, who lament the emptiness in the human heart... There are both kinds.
But the great question is: can the great majority live without sanctities, without these ancient and modern fortresses in which it can rest without doubting, without reconsidering and reflecting?
And not only because the inherited sanctities still speak blindly out of us, but because the human heart, the human psyche, is a favourable soil for sanctities... and on every uprooted sanctity another one immediately grows up.
Only individual people — the “holiest” in our human language — can live without sanctities, that is, in a perpetual intellectual revolution, in constant inquiry and learning.
But the great majority of people, it seems, must from time to time rest in faith, in sanctities — in the dark psychic calm of an ancient temple, or at the grave of a great revolutionary and destroyer of sanctities.
Searches of Pockets

[Poland — taxation; article reprinted from Kurier Warszawski.] The decree on conducting searches of people's pockets is surely a result of the mood among the tax authorities, which is full of suspicion that the taxpayer is able to pay, only he does not want to. The numerous, unusually tragic facts, which establish very clearly for everyone that the taxpayer already finds himself at the edge of the abyss — when only one way out remains: suicide, liquidation of the business, complete ruin; when a man of strength, able to work, suddenly becomes a useless[?] person and is pushed into the great army of the unemployed and hungry — all this, which is sad and horrifying to an objectively thinking person, is not sufficiently convincing proof for the psychology and mentality of the representatives of the tax authorities.
From the facts of real everyday life one can see that tax revenues are weakening and economic life is becoming chaotic. It is hard to defend the principle that among millions of taxpayers there are no dishonest, frivolous people who wish to avoid paying their taxes; but under no circumstances can one demand that, because of the guilt of a small group of individuals, everyone should suffer.
Already now, alarms are being raised from all sides about unusually malicious acts[?] being applied in the personal searches. We do not wish now to verify the significance of these facts, but we hold that the first alarms demand very far-reaching caution in further practice; this is all the more necessary because the broad powers in personal searches can give rise to robberies and abuses. The fact that the "inspectors" are obliged to show their credentials before a personal search is, under our conditions, a tragic fiction. What use is a false credential to a peasant or to a Jewish trader, among whom it also happens that a coloured piece of advertising paper is accepted as a dollar; and what use is a false credential to millions of nervous taxpayers, who may even be able to read but cannot know whether the credential is genuine or forged. In a country in which there are so many forgers of banknotes, of passports and of all kinds of documents, it is so hard [sic, ironic] to make false credentials of the tax offices.
And indeed, our criminals would display unusual incompetence if they did not widely exploit the powers to conduct searches among the population — a population that is to a large extent unaware [of its rights], always frightened and nervous, and seldom capable of sober judgement as to whether it is dealing with an official or simply with a criminal.
Call the police during a personal search? But even in Warsaw the police are too busy to be able to come in time to every call of a citizen who wants to check whether he has before him a genuine or a false bailiff (executor). How many tragic incidents and mistakes may occur because of this.
What a depressed mood the decrees on pocket searches have caused among the population in the towns and villages — the authorities are already informed about it through their representatives, or they will soon learn of it. We cannot recall any decree that has caused so much bitterness and depressed moods among the population. We do not believe that the aim of the authors of the decrees was to bring about such a state of affairs.
If the decree on pocket searches was meant to exert strong pressure on weak taxpayers, we do not believe even for a single minute that the pocket searches will bring a good result. Publicists, and the press in general, are in too close contact with the population not to be able to feel the reality and the actual situation. Besides, the tax authorities do have well-attested reports on the economic situation from the agricultural and economic organizations, based on factual studies of the situation. From this it is surely easy to judge that the poor ability of the masses to pay is not ill will, but the result of a truly critical situation.
Whether the fear that is cast upon the population by means of the decrees on personal searches will lift our economic situation and the ability to pay — this the nearest future will show us. Soon the representatives of economic life, who certainly cannot be accused of opposition to the government nor of pessimism, will be able to voice their opinion on this. Our opinion is that the State and the Treasury (Skarb) will suffer greater harm from it than the benefit expected.

The Jewish Gymnasium in Sosnowiec in New Premises

[Sosnowiec — Education.] After much effort and toil, the administration of the Jewish gymnasium in Sosnowiec has succeeded, in the present time of crisis, in renting for the school a two-storey building which will make it possible to arrange the institution in a modern manner, adapted to the conditions of the new school reform. The building, located in the centre of town yet far from the alarm and noise of the street, consists of 28 comfortable and bright rooms. Work is in full swing to adapt the building to the needs of a secondary school. A thorough renovation is being carried out, and care is being taken that the hygienic conditions for the children be the best.
In the new premises the gymnasium will celebrate the 10th jubilee of its existence. It was fated, however, that the celebration should be somewhat disturbed, on account of a pupil from the Częstochowa Jewish gymnasium who came here a few weeks ago and soon became a weapon in the hands of irresponsible elements who want to hasten world revolution and destroy the Jewish school system — and the 16-year-old pupil, who had barely been at the Sosnowiec gymnasium a couple of weeks, was arrested for communist activity. Self-evidently, although the gymnasium cannot be held responsible for this, the antisemitic press does not stop printing alarming reports about communism in the Jewish gymnasium. That would interest no one — that is what the antisemitic press exists for. But it would be very sad if someone were to be found among "our own", and sometimes even certified Zionists, who would be so shameless as to want to repeat the base libels of the antisemitic press. We are used to the fact that, in order to justify why they send their own child precisely to the non-Jewish school, people spit on the Jewish school, which has earned a name in professional circles as a model school — and this is a generally known thing.
It is therefore to be hoped that with the new year, when the Jewish gymnasium in Sosnowiec moves into the fresh premises, a new, flourishing epoch will begin for the school, because until now the cramped premises were the only obstacle preventing the gymnasium from developing outwardly as it has in the pedagogical field.
It should also be noted that precisely at the time when the incident occurred, the inspector of the Kuratorium [school-district board] was staying at the gymnasium and observed with the greatest admiration the work of the Jewish gymnasium in Sosnowiec. The inspector, Mrs. Dr. Lipska, was present at the meeting of the parents' committee, took part on the same day, Sunday [?] afternoon, in the parents' conference, visited the school four days in a row, and everywhere found only words of satisfaction for the activity of the Jewish gymnasium in Sosnowiec.
Therefore one need not let the celebration be disturbed, and should celebrate in the new premises a double holiday — a house-warming and the 10 years of existence of the gymnasium, which now receives the greatest opportunity for the broadest development.

The Two-Gulden Coin (A Sketch)

[Sketch.] In the morning, as I sat at my table in the dining room eating my breakfast, I suddenly heard a hysterical shriek from the street.
In front of the window stood a peasant cart, surrounded by a bunch of housewives and maidservants, as is the custom, and the fur-clad peasant woman, who sat on the cart with her feet buried in straw, was the one letting out the loud shrieks.
What had happened?
A housewife had haggled with the peasant woman over a rooster for two gulden [złoty], and when they had already agreed on the price and the buyer already wanted to take the purchase, the gentile woman said:
— Well, and the money?
— What do you mean, I already gave it to you!
— Where, when?
— Just now, a silver two-gulden coin.
— But I don't have it!
— But I did give it to you!
And the woman was already holding the rooster in her hand and wanted to leave.
Then the peasant woman broke out shrieking.
A Jewish woman, who told me about it through the open little window, added quietly:
— A goyish woman, a thief!
And at the same moment I heard a Christian maidservant saying to her friend:
— A Jewess (żydówka), a thief!
*
And I thought to myself at that very moment:
— Here is what national estrangement means!
The Jewish woman does not know the soul of the peasant woman, and suspects her of deliberate theft; and the Christian maidservant does not know the soul of the [Jewish] woman, and suspects her of the same.
And the story could have happened not with a lost two-gulden coin but with a lost... child! And it has indeed happened more than once! And how much bloodshed has it brought about?
*
At that same moment the peasant woman fell silent.
What had happened?
They had found the two-gulden coin [misprinted "bildn"] in the straw.
So, too, a lost child is sometimes found...
Avi-Ver.

Oneg Shabbat
Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Toldot

[Weekly Torah portion column — Parashat Toldot and its Haftarah.] The portion.
A) "And the first came forth ruddy" (25:25)
Jacob and Esau divided the worlds between them while still in their mother's womb. Jacob insisted on the World to Come, and Esau took this world for himself; but he could not wait for his share of this world. He sprang out first, red from straining [lit. tearing himself] towards this world... Midrash Rabbah.
—o—
One winter night a Jew knocks at the window of Rabbi Pinchas Horowitz. He is travelling from a fair. Outside the weather is terrible, and at the rabbi's the fire is burning. Warming himself a little by the stove, the Jew sighs:
— Rabbi, this world I no longer have; will I at least have the World to Come?
— See for yourself — Reb Pinchas answers him — for this world you work so hard and bitterly, you travel to fairs in such frosts, and you don't have it. And the World to Come, for which you do not toil at all, you want to have?...
— And further — Reb Pinchas adds — if so, because you get blackened [with toil] you want the World to Come? Then your horse would get to the World to Come sooner; it is standing even now outside in the snow and the frost...
—o—
— People complain — the Chatam Sofer used to say — that they have nothing to live on. But I have never yet heard people complain that they have nothing to die on...
B) "And after that came forth his brother" (ibid., 26)
"Ach" usually means: a brother; but sometimes "ach" also means: a misfortune... (see Sanhedrin 102). Such an "ach" is Esau to Jacob... Nachalat Yaakov.
C) "And the boys grew, and Esau was" (ibid., 27)
Parents usually pay no attention to their children while they are still small. "It's still a child" — people say. But with such an upbringing it mostly[?] happens that "the boys grew — and suddenly — Esau was"; suddenly one looks around and an Esau has grown up, and then it is already too late... Orach Chaim.
D) "Wherefore are ye come unto me, seeing ye hate me" (ibid., 27)
See, Isaac was in Abimelech's land and Abimelech came to him to flatter him; yet Isaac could not bear any flattery and simply asked Abimelech and his captain of the host: you hate me, after all — why have you come to me?... To'aliyot of the Ralbag.
E) "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau" (27:22)
"The voice is the voice of Jacob" — Jews pray for a year of blessing, a year of trade; "but the hands are the hands of Esau" — and Esau takes it all into his own hands... Like two beggars, a sighted one and a blind one, who go about collecting alms. The blind one begs for alms, people pity him and give, and the sighted one takes... Yeriot ha-Ohel.
—o—
"Ha-kol kol Yaakov" [written defectively] — the "kol" is lacking, without a vav: when the hands of Esau multiply deeds, the voice of Jacob is lacking, it stands to reason[?]... Tzelota de-Avraham.
F) "Be lord over thy brethren" (ibid., 29)
You will be held a rich man "over your brethren" because you belong to your brethren, because you are a Jew. A Jew as such is a rich man — he must pay the biggest taxes... Ezrat Yisrael.
G) "Bless me, even me also, O my father" (ibid., 34)
Uncle Esau's position was a hard one. Before Isaac he had always posed as a righteous man in the field, whom the world does not concern at all — and now suddenly he cries that he has been robbed of the blessings of this world. Like the man from whom a stolen object was stolen... he has to keep his mouth shut and shout in disguise. Esau, too, just cried: "Bless me, even me also, O my father" — but which blessings he meant, he was ashamed to say... Ohel Yaakov.
H) "Of the dew of heaven, and of the fat places of the earth" (ibid., 28)
In the days of the old Kotzker [rebbe of Kock] there was once a great glut of cheap goods, and the merchants complained that trade was suffering from it and one could do no business.
The Kotzker replies:
— Don't worry. God, who helps the poor in times of dearness, will help the rich in times of cheapness...
Haftarah.
I) "Was not Esau Jacob's brother… yet I loved Jacob" (Malachi 1)
This is truly a love that upsets the normal order: even when "Esau is Jacob's brother", when Jacob fraternises with Esau and becomes too closely related by marriage to him — God still loves Jacob... Sha'ar Bat Rabbim.
J) "He walked with Me in peace and uprightness, and did turn many away from iniquity" (ibid.)
This is the way: not with Cossack tricks and by force to bring another back to repentance, but in peace and uprightness... Misgeret ha-Sha'ar.
Let Us Talk It Over a Little! What We Expected of the Jewish Sports Movement in Zagłębie and What We Have Achieved

[Sport — Zagłębie; opinion.]
2.
In this second article we want precisely to talk over whether anyone who possesses a sense of responsibility can say with a clear conscience that the Jewish sports movement today has a meaning, and whether it strives toward a definite goal — toward the goal which the pioneers of the movement set themselves 20 years ago?
By no means.
We know that many of today's “mod[e]s” [?] in the sports movement will shrug their shoulders and will not want to understand what we are talking about; therefore we want to say everything clearly and openly. We have lost every idea, because we have ceased to be a mass movement, because our associations have begun to function and exist only for individual sportsmen whom nature has not stinted and has rewarded with talent in this field; our associations have become entrepreneurs of smaller and larger circuses, which are kept and trained for performances before a large public.
This has been said especially of football, where there is a genuine stock exchange, where players are bought and sold, and in such transactions money is taken not only by the player himself but also by the association that sells the player. The football federation has already arranged things so that the football player becomes the property of the association. That would not be bad if the associations and the managements were conscientious, but it is not so: players are traded just like foreign currency on the black market. The player himself knows his worth, and he becomes and [sic] is utterly demoralized. He tears himself away from his work, becomes a professional; he plays because he gets money, and therefore it makes no difference to him where he plays — the main thing is that he should get as high a salary as possible and as big a bonus as possible for every goal scored.
It has, after all, happened more than once, and will surely still happen quite often, that players who today played in blue-and-white shirts and defended the “national pride” in a Jewish club, played tomorrow in a Polish club and defended the amaranth-and-white colours against yesterday's national pride — and all this only because they got more money.
It has, after all, happened that someone who defended proletarian sport against bourgeois sport did exactly the opposite the next day — not because he had changed his convictions, but because he had “hired himself out” to another club and his club of yesterday had received “transfer money” for him.
The worst of it is that everything we write here is already known to all; these are no longer sensations and revelations, these are by now simple matters which the young generation thinks must be so, because it did not stand with us at our beginning and does not know how much self-sacrifice was put into founding our associations.
All these things we have written about poison everything around, and even the smallest provincial townlet is already infected with them. How many associations in the provinces that have only a football team [drużyna] can tell of such deeds from their own practice — and this practice repels from us all those elements in Jewish society on whose support we had counted and whom we had hoped to win for our movement.
Our call is therefore: back to the idea. Of course we have not yet exhausted the whole problem; we will return to it in the next article.

When Can a Registration Card Replace a Patent?

[Trade and industry — taxation; patents.]
Every independent enterprise is obliged to purchase a separate patent [trade licence, świadectwo przemysłowe].
There are many industrial enterprises which at the same time run sales points for their own products. The question then arises whether such sales points are treated as independent enterprises or as component parts of the industrial enterprises proper.
And here one must come to the following conclusions: if an industrial enterprise at the same time conducts a sale of its own products wholesale, i.e. in larger amounts to merchants or manufacturers, such a sales point need not be regarded as an independent enterprise, and consequently it need not have a separate patent.
On the other hand, if a sale takes place retail, or even wholesale but together with other people's products, it is already treated as an independent enterprise, for which a special patent must therefore be purchased.
As regards the number of wholesale sales points that can be treated as non-independent enterprises, it must be established that in the same town where the factory proper is located, many such wholesale sales points may be run; outside the factory town an industrial enterprise is entitled to conduct wholesale selling exclusively at one single point. But as soon as an industrial enterprise conducts wholesale selling in several towns, all these wholesale sales points are regarded as independent enterprises and they must provide themselves with separate patents.
Incidentally it should be noted that [sic] even qualified wholesale sales points (not independent enterprises) are likewise not exempt from the obligation to provide themselves with industrial certificates. True, they need not purchase separate patents, but they are obliged to provide themselves with registration cards.
When we speak of wholesale selling of one's own products without a patent, on the basis of a mere registration card [karta rejestracyjna], we mean selling outside the factory. Selling one's own products retail and in small amounts on the premises of the very place where the industrial enterprise proper is located is not regarded as a separate enterprise. Consequently one need not purchase a special patent for such selling, nor even a registration card.
On this occasion it is also worth drawing attention to the existing difference between a sales point and a warehouse.
A warehouse means one or several united premises [“obikatsies”, as printed] belonging to one trading or industrial enterprise, serving exclusively for storing, drying, cleaning, sorting, reloading or packing goods, raw materials, materials, possibly machines or other implements; in any case no business transactions whatsoever may be concluded in such a warehouse, and it may not have the character of a trading enterprise at all.
Every such warehouse must be provided with a separate registration card.
At the same time one must also remember that on the basis of a patent of the 1st trading category one may keep such warehouses throughout the whole territory of the state; a second-category trading patent entitles one to possess an unlimited number of such warehouses, but only within the same town where the given trading enterprise is located. A patent of the 3rd category permits keeping not more than 2 warehouses, and that too only in the same building where the business is located.
Trading enterprises of the 4th category are altogether forbidden to possess warehouses.
Y. Einfeld.

Winter.
A popular medical talk.

We call winter the time when snow falls.
In winter one must dress warmly; by this we mainly mean an overcoat: men wear “hooked” [?] (“gehakte”) coats with plush collars, and women — little brown coats with karakul collars, or imitation karakul, so-called “parzielki” [?]. Patents [trade licences] for craftsmen. — Sosnowiec rabbinate against selling kosher meat in the market halls.

[Economy — Taxes.] Patents [trade licences] for craftsmen.
Craftsmen who work alone must hold 8th-category patents. We draw attention to the fact that under the new law one already had to hold patents in 1932 even when one had no journeyman; whoever does not buy a patent for the new year may be written up with a protocol [citation].
Craftsmen who employ 4 persons, counting the owner and family members, must hold the 8th category.
Craftsmen doing hand-work who employ more than 4 workers and not more than 9 workers must hold the 7th category.
If one works with machines, even without motors, one may keep only 7 workers on a 7th category.
For hand-work with 7 to 15 workers one must hold the sixth category; machine-work with 7 to 10 workers — sixth category.
On the fifth category one may have, for hand-work, 15 to 50 workers, and for machine-work 10 to 25 workers.

[Dąbrowa — kehilla.] The new kehilla budget is suffering a „gilgul mehilot“ (an underground wandering of the dead). The board sent the budget to the council. The council, after a thorough „investigation“, sent it back to the board, and the board back to the council. But the etat (communal tax) payers will profit from this „expedition“: thanks to the fact that there is no domestic peace between the board and the council, this year's budget has been reduced by 14 thousand złoty.
At Sunday's meeting of the board the budget already adopted by the council was considered; after a short discussion it was decided to reduce the pensions of the rabbi by 10 per cent and of the officials by 15 per cent. The board also cancelled the subsidies for artisans' courses, the „manifesto“ that residents of Reden may immerse free of charge, and the subsidy for poor artisans for patents (trade licences).
At the meeting board member (dozor) Mr. Granitman proposed a resolution that the Jewish community in Dąbrowa declares its solidarity with the Jewish university students, who showed self-sacrifice during the anti-Jewish excesses.
The president, Mr. Neufeld, brought in a resolution expressing a sharp protest against the attacks of the Endek youth, in which the Jewish kehilla in Dąbrowa appeals to the authorities to punish those guilty of the excesses.
Mr. Neufeld's resolution was adopted.
———

During the past week the gmina distributed 250 korzec of potatoes to poor families.

Who Raised the Kehilla Budget in Dąbrowa? (A Letter to the Editor)

[Dąbrowa — kehilla; letter to the editor.] Esteemed Mr. Editor!
In connection with the report that appeared in the „Zagl. Tsayt.“ no. 49 of this year, „The revue [?] scenes at the budget meeting of the Dąbrowa kehilla council“, I ask you to print the following letter:
1) It is not true that the kehilla council enlarged the budget; on the contrary, it is true that the board drew up for the year 1933 a budget of 126 935 zł., of which the etat alone came to 62.[—]95 zł., and the council at its plenary meeting of the 27th of this month reduced the budget to 101,025 zł., and of that the etat to 36,485 zł.
2) It is not true that the board planned to reduce the pensions; on the contrary, it is true that in the board's budget there figured increased items for several kehilla employees, compared with what they received last year, and it was the kehilla council that reduced the pensions.
Finally, allow me to draw attention to the following detail, which throws light on the „conditions“ under which one has to work in the new Dąbrowa kahal:
After the final adoption by the kehilla council of the reduced budget, the president of the board declared that he was submitting a votum separatum and that he would make efforts „there where one must“ to have the budget that the board had planned approved...
With thanks and respect,
Herzl Liberman
President of the kehilla council in Dąbrowa.
