The Antisemites and Our "Maskes" [Masks]

[Essay — Antisemitism.]
(Wherein lies the strength of antisemitism, and how does one confront it?)
It often happens to a person that he is in a bad mood, that this or that undertaking does not succeed for him, that he loses money — he becomes beside himself, and the results are not impressive. At such a moment one gets agitated and begins to look for the guilty; and if one is oneself to blame, if one is a schlimazel, one will certainly not throw the faults onto oneself — that is simply human nature — and so one begins to look for the guilty in entirely different spheres, just so as to have someone onto whom to throw the faults for which one is oneself to blame.
This is said with regard to our "kind-hearted" Endek organ [of the Endecja, National Democrats]. It is no longer a secret to anyone that things there are not so cheerful[?]. At such a moment one would gladly grab hold even of a smooth wall, just to climb up to the proper height; but when one sees that all the combinations do not work out, and one falls ever lower, one loses one's balance completely and scribbles about what the world stands on — nonsense that never rose and never flew.
When Będzin a few months ago received a new notary [rejent] and the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" printed a notice that he is a liberal man, that very "Kurier Zachodni" stood on guard and made sure that such a stain should, God forbid, not fall on the said person.
Usually people in Zagłębie live in peace with antisemitism. Christians know quite well that with a Jewish firm one can get something done, and that the calculation works out better with Jews. It [the paper] cannot bear to see how people live calmly with people, do business among themselves, and one makes a living from the other. So it wants — this Endek editorial office — to stir up a storm by every means, so that for a long time now it has set itself the goal of inciting without end. Nearly every issue that appears is soaked with a certain dose[?] of poison and inflammatory material, and the less one achieves with the agitation, the more courage one takes to provoke an upheaval. Who does not see what stinging slogans are printed there, in which the question is asked: have you already provided for yourself, while you feed a superfluous 3 million strangers? Yes, they speak to the heart in a tone of moral preaching, they awaken feelings, they storm and tear and overturn worlds, just to carry out what they are after.
They have set about smearing, right and left, everything that is Jewish; as soon as one sees a joint activity between Jews and Christians, it is ridiculed; as soon as one sees a united action being carried out, they do not rest — they begin to rampage and to overturn worlds. Still good that all this amounts to a storm in a glass of water, because the paper is not read by the masses; the broad strata of the Polish population have long ignored it.
But it has another virtue, which consists in this: its readers are ours — our brethren, the Children of Israel, read it with great relish and delight in the spiritual food with which they are fed. Apparently they take pleasure in the hate articles, poisonous notices and screaming advertisements which imply that a Jew is treyf and a Jewish merchant is a swindler. Moreover, our "maskes" [masks] are not content with merely reading the paper, but push their way in with advertisements as well. The Sunday issues, which contain the largest dose of hate material, carry a sizeable number of Jewish advertisements. Yes, our assimilated and national "maskes" are represented there in a most honourable fashion.
Yes, many a time one laughs bitterly into one's fists, when one reads through a slogan that screams "gevalt", that one may not buy anywhere else but in a Catholic firm — and right after the notice there is the advertisement of a Jewish firm, which is to say: look, here is who wants to get you into his paws and cheat you! The editorial office simply needs the advertisement in order to show that the business has a mezuzah and that it belongs to a Jew — and the Jew really does offer his shoulders at once and shows: here I am, beat me as much as you like — and for that one pays extra into the bargain; so they really make a golden business.
These are the results of the hate articles. The more inflammatory material they provide, the better Jewish advertisements they receive. It is interesting: not long ago we came across a notice in which the relatives of the deceased inform the readers that on such-and-such a date and at such-and-such a time a memorial service will take place at the Jewish cemetery. That is the kind of absurdity one can be brought to among us. There is no doubt that the antisemitic gang of pens rolls with laughter when they read through such a condolence, and when they remember that they earn an income from it, they may surely laugh.
Incidentally, the Jewish advertisements lift the business, because this is a good argument for obtaining non-Jewish advertisements: then they have a justified claim towards their Catholic readers who do not give advertisements, and they can prove to them: see, even the "Żydki", in whose faces we simply spit, rush to print their advertisements on the pages of our paper; and if Jews give — you know that they know what they are doing; they would not give a goy money for nothing.
It is quite possible that if they have enough Christian advertisements, they will then manage altogether without the Jewish ones. And one fine day, wishing to remain free of Jews, they will announce that they have no connection whatsoever with Jews and no longer accept any Jewish advertisements, as was the case before the war. What will these poor "maskes" do then? Who will then take pity on them, and to whom will they push themselves then?
Yes, a decent Christian, an honest Pole, will have no dealings with such sold souls; they will not take a dishonest newspaper into their hands. But among us people have fallen so low that there is no shame. We are insulted, we are disgraced, our feelings are humiliated to the utmost, our honesty and decency are mocked and our poverty is derided, blood libels are made against us so that we be looked upon with disgust and contempt. It is not enough that among us no one reacts to all this, not enough that we do not demand accountability for degrading the Jewish community — on the contrary, all sorts of "maskes" turn up among us, who go out with a fawning smile to meet the antisemitic squire and give him a hearty "yasher koach" for the disgrace and the libels, and in recognition he is rewarded for it.
All our assorted "ma yafit" [obsequious] little Jews, the modern as well as the backward, will be happy when some Christian lad deigns to smile at them — a lad to whom they show respect and courtesy and to whom they carry their "good morning", while that one does not want it at all.
The "maskes" will promptly argue to you that we must not separate ourselves, that we live in the 20th century and must be democratically minded, and that our views must be democratic, modernizing. But they do not see that we are shunned only because we are Jews, and that in the antisemite's eyes every Jew, whatever outlook he may belong to, is a devil, an unwanted element that must be exterminated by whatever means. Our "maskes" do not see at all in which direction the antisemitic policy of extermination is heading.
Here in Zagłębie and Upper Silesia it is quiet and calm: people live together and suffer together, one understands the other, without distinction of race and religion to which he belongs. [Yet] the hidden individuals want with all their might to force their way in, and with their incendiary material they want to kindle a hellish fire that will flare up and from which they can draw sustenance. All this our "maskes" do not see; their small-headed brains do not grasp it, and they think that with their flattery they have hit the bird [hit the mark].
One often loses heart when one sees [printed "nisht"] how they want to annihilate us, how they want to lead us off the straight path, how, because of what we are, we have no one to sit down at table with. Very well — against enemies one knows how to guard oneself; they know [as printed; read: we know they] want to see us faring badly. Worse it is with our own "maskes", who in the Catholic camp want to be more papal than the Pope, and among us want to play the role of devoted Jews and great men.
Dr. Papuri.

Oneg Shabbat
Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Vayeshev

[Weekly Torah portion column — Parashat Vayeshev and the Haftarah of Shabbat Hanukkah.] The portion.
A) "And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings" (37:1)
At the end of the previous portion we are told of so many chiefs of Esau by whom Jacob was surrounded, and yet — among all these Esau-like[?] neighbours: "And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings." He conducted himself like his father, in the traditional Jewish way... Rabbi Zvi Hirsch Kalischer.
—o—
The well-known pious magnate Moses Montefiore was once travelling by train, first class, in a compartment with a number of Christian noblemen and also some assimilated Jews. When the time for Minhah came, Montefiore stood up to pray Minhah. The assimilationists could not calm down: to stand up among gentile noblemen and pray? A Jewish chutzpah!...
After praying, Montefiore goes over to the band of assimilationists:
— Perhaps one of you can change a thousand-pound note?
They shrug their shoulders.
— And perhaps a five-hundred?
Again they shrug their shoulders.
— And perhaps a hundred?
— Not that either.
— Beggars! — Montefiore exclaims — you don't have a penny to your name, and you mock a Jew when he prays. Well, if you were at least rich men, so be it... but beggars like you...
B) "And Joseph brought evil report of them unto their father" (ibid., 2)
Their deeds are all the uglier because — "unto their father": because they have such a father as Jacob... Tzvi la-Tzaddik.
C) "And he made him a coat of many colours" (ibid., 3)
The Gemara says: "Why are the scholars of Babylon distinguished [by their dress]? — Because they are not learned in Torah." That is, those who are not learned in Torah are precisely the ones who like to dress like scholars and put on airs of learned men, but the true scholars dress plainly and make nothing of themselves..
And because Joseph was a "bar ḥakim" (a wise son) and could thereby draw upon himself his brothers' envy, his father specially dressed him in a coat of many colours, which was to show that he was precisely not a scholar — for if he were, he would surely not dress in silks... Torat Moshe.
—o—
The Maggid of Dubno once came to a town where he was not treated well, and he put on his Sabbath clothes. They asked him: what is the meaning of this? — He answered:
The Gemara says: "Why are the scholars in Babylon distinguished? — Because they are not learned in Torah." If they are not learned in Torah, why does it call them scholars [printed: "talmudei-hakhamim"] just before? But the meaning is: "because they are not bnei Torah" [printed: "torat"] — the people of Babylon are not learned in Torah, and because the townspeople cannot study, the scholars must dress handsomely: since the Babylonian ignoramuses will not honour them for their Torah, let them at least honour the scholars for their clothing...
D) "Shalt thou indeed reign over us?" (ibid., 8)
"Ha-melekh" — if you can rule and reign over yourself — "timlokh aleinu" — only then can you become a ruler over others...
Reb Zusha of Anipoli.
E) "And they conspired against him to slay him" (ibid., 18)
"They set the dogs on him." Midrash.
The Gemara says (Pesahim 118): "Whoever speaks slander deserves to be thrown to the dogs," because dogs, although bold by nature, can sometimes restrain themselves from barking, whereas the slanderer will never manage[?] it...
Kiflayim le-Tushiya.
F) "And he was in the house of his master... the Lord was with him... the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand" (39:3)
When a man is too well off, he forgets God. Likewise, when he is too badly off, his troubles also make him forget God. Joseph was with God while finding himself in both situations: when he was a prosperous man and when he was a slave in Potiphar's house...
Binah le-Itim.
The Haftarah of Shabbat Hanukkah.
G) "And he shall bring forth the head stone" (Zechariah 2 [so printed; the verse is Zechariah 4:7])
"This is the stone of Jacob, as it is said: And Jacob rose up early in the morning and took the stone." Yalkut Shimoni.
This stone of Jacob, the stone on which our father Jacob leaned when he found himself forlorn in the wilderness, without the slightest hope, fleeing from Esau to Laban, from one enemy to the other, when everything rebelled against him, even the stones under his head quarrelled — and yet he then saw his heavenly dream: that stone is the "head stone", the symbol of the Jewish people... Hegyonot ha-RaMaH.
H) "Be silent, all flesh, before the Lord" (ibid.)
"For He is roused out of His holy habitation — like a hen shaking itself out of the ashes."
The hen, when she rolls in the ashes, also gets a certain pleasure out of it. Such pleasure we get from rolling about in various cultural dunghills... But just as "betzim de-sapna me-ar'a" [eggs of the earth?] have no power of development, so too the product of such a culture.
Rabbi Moshe Horowitz.
Old Jewish 'Main Privileges' in the Former Polish Kingdom *)

[History — Polish Jewry.] Dr. Moshe Schorr [Mojżesz Schorr].
2.
Apart from this main privilege, which has 24 points in our collection, and which from the middle of the 15th century was the "great privilege scroll" for all the Jews of Poland, as can be seen[?] from the signatures of several later kings on it — the volume also contains the gist of several later important privileges, from the middle of the 16th century up to the last king Stanisław, which likewise touch on the fundamentals of the political and economic situation of all the Jews of Poland and are counted together with the preceding one in a single numbering: they have 17 points (25 — 45); from this it appears that these privileges were a kind of novellae and improvements to that main privilege of Casimir the Great. The last part contains eleven privileges of the 16th and 17th centuries, which concern only the Kraków kehilla. That main privilege of Casimir the Great and its content have occupied everyone who studies the history of the Jews in Poland, especially Dr. Yitzhak Schiper [Ignacy Schiper] in his Hebrew translation and adaptation of Graetz's History (see there. Especially important are those novellae and improvements (25 — 42), which stem mostly from the time of the kings Zygmunt August (1548—1572), Stefan Batory (1576-1586) and Władysław the Fourth (1633—1648). It is only these important novellae that we will discuss here, because they have a certain bearing on the history of our own days as well. They show us clearly that the old Polish kingdom protected the Jews much more than today's; many of these novellae deserve to be read out publicly by our deputies from the Sejm rostrum, to prove to the legislators that with their Jew-hating laws they are not following the tradition of their fathers; perhaps they will repent...
In the following paragraphs the content of the "privileges scroll" is given in its order, in a literal translation from the Latin original:
25. "When a person, or a town, oppresses the Jews, or incites to pogroms, or takes part in them, the pledge of 10,000[?] Polish marks deposited there is forfeited; in addition, a fine of the same sum is imposed on the town and on the magistrate, if he does not stop the excesses and does not defend the Jews. Whoever kills a Jew is punished with the death penalty, and his entire property is confiscated for the king's treasury (copied from the decree of King Zygmunt August, issued in Warsaw on 23 May, 1571, apart from the general rights-privilege).
26. "When a Jew in a loan matter provides a sufficient guarantor (surety), the voivode may not put him in prison; if he does not provide a guarantor, he shall arrest him in an ordinary prison, not in an underground chamber. The guarantor must be a decent, honest and well-to-do Jew, not only a Christian. The voivode shall allow an appeal against his verdict in a claim above 20 gulden (from the aforementioned king in Piotrków on 7 August 1564).
27, A Christian creditor may not press the Jew to collect the debt from him unless he applies to the judge. If the Jew cannot pay his debt in cash, he shall pawn his property with a Jew, not with a Christian (from the same king in Wilno, 11 August, 1551).
28. The Jews may choose for themselves a rabbi (doctor) or a dayan; if a Jew will not obey him, or will not pay him due respect, that Jew shall be brought before the king's court and punished with the death penalty and confiscation of property. The dayan (rabbi) is not subject to any authority except the king, so that it be easier for him to perform his service (from King Stefan in Warsaw on 19 February 1578).
29. The Jews have equal rights with the burghers and enjoy their privileges; they are subject to the king, except in private matters.
30. It shall be seen to that the burghers do not prevent the Jews from hiring craftsmen to build houses. If there is any dispute about this, the voivode shall decide.
31. The voivode or his deputy may not sit in judgment without the attendance of the heads of the kehilla, without hearing their opinion, which they must express in due order. The sworn secretary of the court may not be chosen or appointed before he [i.e. one] informs the head of the kehilla, [and] he shall give his consent.
32. In order to give the Jews a better source of livelihood and existence, they are permitted to engage in crafts without any hindrance.
33) When a Jew converts and marries a Christian woman and has children with her, these children may not be made "bilkher" [more favoured? / cheaper? — ambiguous word as printed] than his children by his first, Jewish wife, especially regarding inheritance.
34. The Jews are obliged to record the items pawned with them in a book at the voivode's, so that thefts can be detected.
35. The Jews are not obliged to swear standing on a pig's skin or in any other manner, but only on a Torah scroll, or at the synagogue door ("shul-tir"), as the state documents say.
36. On Sabbath and holidays the Jews may not be summoned to court, as is already stated in Bolesław's privilege and Casimir's confirmation. (28).
37. When a Jew dies, his wife has priority over the creditors regarding her dowry, which is recorded in the books of the voivode or of the town. Only what remains after the creditors are paid falls to the heirs (nos. 28 and 37 are copied from the privilege of Stefan Batory of 15 December 1576, which was later confirmed by King Władysław).
38. The Jews may trade in the Christian shops in all kinds of goods; like the Christians, they may freely leave the town.
39. A Christian may not take on the guardianship of Jewish children. That belongs to the rabbi and the Jewish elders.
40. When a Christian summons a Jew to court, the heads of the kehilla may attend the court, on condition that they obtain permission for this from our Tribunal court, as their earlier privileges specify in every detail. (38 and 40 — by King Jan Kazimierz in Warsaw on 13 June 1661).
41. In loan transactions with people of another kind (that is, when the lender is a Christian and the recipient a Jew), (the lender) may not transfer the debt to the name of a more powerful person (a Christian, of course). Rather, he must come himself with a claim, according to the law of Israel. Likewise, the Jewish lenders may not transfer their Jewish debts to the names of more powerful persons; rather they must themselves summon the debtors to the court — as is proper and as that same privilege gives to understand.
All these laws were confirmed by King Michał Wiśniowiecki at the Sejm in Warsaw on the 5th of November 1669. After King Michał they were signed by King Jan Sobieski, at the coronation Sejm in Kraków on 28 April 1676; after him by King August III of Saxony at the Sejm session in Warsaw on 7 December 1735; the last to sign was King Stanisław August.

Tax Assessment (A word about the new assessment committees)

[Dąbrowa — economy and taxes.] We now stand before the confirmation of new members of the assessment committees for income tax, which will begin their activity on 1 January 1933. That means new people are taking over the assessment of the main taxes the citizen must pay. It is therefore worth dwelling on the way things are run when each merchant or artisan is judged — how high the tax he is to pay in the given year should be. The economic organizations must pay more attention to matters that until now have been underrated [sic; a full stop seems to be missing between the sentences].
One must not forget that the work of the assessment committees cannot be compared to the category of prestigious functions in the public sense; the work is hard, especially when it is not properly appreciated by the Finance Office (tax office), which is dissatisfied with those members who have the courage to defend the livelihoods of the taxpayers.
Unfortunately, the representatives of the merchants' bodies for the most part do not take account of the importance of their tasks on the assessment committees. The statistics of recent years show the committees' casual attitude toward their duties.
On the basis of the materials collected by it, it is established that there are members who assess and come forward with self-sacrifice only when their friends and their families are being dealt with — for whom they sacrifice themselves so that, God forbid, no injustice befalls them — and at the expense of the majority of taxpayers they do indeed manage to protect their "gante"[?], and often their voters too... Not to mention that when merchants or craftsmen who once offended the honour of the assessors are judged, then the whole matter "lies in their left sidelock" [idiom: they couldn't care less]... and the number of "victims" is great.
And the question arises: is it permissible that such people should be defenders of the Jewish merchant class, already so ruined? Have the merchants' bodies ever considered to whom they entrust the fate of their members?
The practice of recent years has also shown that the assessment committees consisted of elements that are entirely unsuitable and did not have the proper authority that the finance offices would have to reckon with their opinions.
Therefore a sacred duty lies on the merchants' organizations: in compiling the new lists of candidates, they must think seriously and delegate people who deserve the fullest trust — people able to defend with pride the vital ("bloody") interests of the taxpayers, people precisely acquainted with the critical situation of the broad Jewish masses, who know what each person does for a living, where he lives and what his material situation looks like, since the moment someone suffers an injustice he is utterly ruined.
This, in brief strokes, is my opinion on this topical question, and it is a duty that meetings of merchants be held to express their demands as to whom to entrust their vital interests for a term of several years.
B. Rechnic,
town councillor (Ratman) in Dąbrowa.
Great Inventions the World Laughed At

[Science and technology — feature.] Special for the Zaglembier Tsaytung. By Z. Haber, Vienna.
Several hundred new inventions have already been registered for the Leipzig Fair, which will open at the end of March 1933. In a large pavilion of its own they will show what the human mind has been capable of creating in the last half year.
Without any doubt it will turn out that a large part of the inventions have no great value at all, and that years of work by people who invested all their strength, money and blood in order to show the great world something new will prove to have been entirely in vain. Surely only some of the inventions that make their way from the Leipzig Fair Office to all the world's centres will find buyers.
But if one looks at the truly great inventions that dominate the world today, and we read in the archives of the Leipzig Fair Office, we see that almost all the greatest inventions were at first laughed at, and the inventors suffered plenty of troubles and torments before it came to be recognized that their invention was a blessing for mankind.
When the inventors of the railway announced that they wanted to run their wagons on steel rails, it provoked wild laughter throughout the entire technical world. All the technical celebrities declared that it was sheer madness... The greatest French physicist of that time, Bernaail [Bernoulli? — as printed], proved with mathematical precision that there could not possibly be steam power strong enough to move wheels on rails. This mathematical treatise received the first prize of the French Academy of Sciences... Nevertheless, about two years later steam engines were running on steel rails...
Another physics genius in Berlin spoke out against "the foolish idea of steam railways," because the powerful steam needed to drive a train "no person or animal will be able to bear," and all around people would drop like straw...
And the Austrian Emperor Ferdinand, whose advice was sought on whether to build a railway in Austria, answered:
"What good is a railway, when even the carters drive empty"...
Things went no better when they wanted to introduce a ship with steam. The English professor Lardner gave the opinion that "one could cross the sea faster with human power than with steam"... He wrote this in 1817, and only two years later, in 1819, the first steamship, the "Savannah," crossed the sea...
People laughed a great deal at the inventor of gas for lighting streets or homes. The French engineer Lebon toiled for years wanting to prove how good it is to light with gas, but almost the whole world laughed at him and considered him a madman. In 1804 he actually died in a madhouse, where he had been locked up because of his "crazy"[?] ideas... Only in 1806 did they begin introducing gas lamps in Manchester, and in Paris they were first lit only in 18:8 [sic; probably 1818]...
In 1885 the inventor of mantle lamps for "Alier" gas [Auer — as printed] gave a lecture on his invention before a large audience of experts. A mishap befell him: the mantle crumbled and could not burn. The audience really wanted to trample him and shouted that he would be put in prison if he went on swindling the world like this... And already in 1891 there was hardly a single country in the world where gas was not burning with "Alier" mantles.
On 9 April 1877 Edison had his newest invention, the phonograph, demonstrated at the Paris Academy of Sciences. The apparatus was shown by Edison's best collaborator, Dr. Ozel [as printed]. A speech of greeting by Edison himself had been recorded on the apparatus. Hardly had the apparatus begun to speak when the president of the Academy, Professor Bouillaud, went up to the platform and from there threw down Dr. Ozel together with the apparatus, shouting that Dr. Ozel dared to deceive the whole audience: "Everyone can see that we are dealing here with a ventriloquist"... Nothing helped; Dr. Ozel had to leave with the phonograph.
Only a few months later Edison sent a phonograph to Paris, which Dr. Bouillaud set up himself and saw that it was no ventriloquist's trick...
As late as 1898 Count Zeppelin was regarded as the greatest swindler, who wanted to persuade the world that "with his bird one will be able to fly"...
In 1906, when he showed his "bird" to the military administration in Berlin and presented his plans, the then German War Minister wrote a report about it to the German Kaiser, in which he writes:
"Count Zeppelin is a fool who wants to persuade us that with his apparatus one will be able to fly"...
Nevertheless, already in 1913 the very same German War Minister flew on that apparatus together with that "crazy" Count Zeppelin...
For the Miracles…

[Humour and satire — Hanukkah.] “The Dreidel” (Dos dreydl) — in place of the “Cooking Ladle” (Der kokh-lefl), in honour of Hanukkah, by Ben Amotz.

“For the miracles and for the deliverances” —
Who needs them?
How long is the measure — to live on miracles?
To feed and refresh oneself on miracles?

“For the miracles and for the deliverances” —
We are driven out of schools and out of shops.
All borders are closed,
Decrees spring up like mushrooms.

We rely on miracles
And are ourselves weak as children —
So we stretch our neck to the slaughterer
Like the dumb, mute cattle...

“These candles” — oh, the little candles!
How dearly they cost us!
We — we burn tiny little candles,
They — they kindle hellish fire.

“These candles” — holy, holy,
In every little candle — a soul...
“Avenge the blood of Your servants”!
Sweet and dear is revenge.

Yes, revenge, oh, revenge!
For us it is merely a phrase;
The revenge of the weak —
Has no foundation and no base.

“For the miracles” — boycott, hatred,
All around us on every side;
Time changes and shifts,
Only for us — the old times...

“For the miracles” — long is the list:
Pharaoh, Haman and Amalek...
Spain and Ukraine as well,
Now — Hitler’s campaign...

“So, in the days of” — and what now?
Are we any better off now?
The pig crawls onto the altar
And the enemy’s knife gleams.

“In the days of Mattathias” — and now?
Does not the same Greek still live?
Is it not the same Jacob?
Is it not the same Laban?

Come over here, fine Hitler,
Are you any better than the Greeks?
With the pig, just as once before,
You do crawl, you do crawl...

“For the miracles” — Jew, how long?
We lack a standing in life.
How much is the measure — on miracles
To fly and hover in the air?

“For the miracles and for the deliverances” —
Ah! How dearly they cost us!
We — we burn little candles,
And the world — its hellish fire.
Hanukkah Gelt

Pigs Are Getting Dearer

[Humour and satire — Zagłębie.] As the “Cooking Ladle” has learned, pigs will soon become dearer. The cause of the fall in prices was that there came to be a glut of pigs; for example, Zagłębie possessed 3,000 rich men.. that is to say, three thousand pigs... not counting certain landlords... and with the “urushand” [?] with certain communal activists... we have had here until now a thousand [?] pigs... so prices did indeed fall. But today, in a time of crisis, when rich men turn into paupers overnight, houses go to auction one after another and there are fewer pigs every day... — prices will inevitably rise: we will have dear rich men, dear communal activists, and pigs will become dear...

How People Groan Today

[Humour and satire — the Depression.]
A merchant:
So groans a merchant today:
Dear Father, sweet Father,
I wait not for any customer
But only for the bailiff.

A doctor:
They don’t pay for visits,
They just tell me to “remember” it [put it on the tab];
That’s the kind of time it has become —
People don’t want to be ill.

A tailor:
Who needs clothes today?
Only old stuff has to be sewn;
It’s a holiday in the workshop
When a garment needs turning.

A shoemaker:
Once shoes were still made,
And now — a calamity, Father;
All you see in the workshop today
Is a patch being put on a shoe.

A carter:
Who needs a little horse today,
Who needs the harness today,
When the autos run so fast? —
So groans the carter.

A matchmaker:
A lament from us matchmakers:
We’re no longer needed,
Every maiden and every lad
Must bury themselves on their own.

An actor:
Where can one find those times
When tickets used to run short?
Now the gallery is empty,
No couplets help.

A thief:
Empty are the pockets,
Dark is my world;
Nowhere today to “work” (“irken”),
The suckers (yoldn) have no money.

A restaurateur:
Once people ate heartily [?],
Drank beer and brandy;
Today water too counts as a drink,
And a bread roll one can only wink at.

An editor:
Once people would buy a newspaper,
And everyone would pay;
Today people only want to read,
But nobody buys.

— — —

So everyone groans today,
Each in his own way;
There isn’t a grosz left today,
Nothing to buy with.

Dovid Spivak.

The terrible dream of an Endek editor.

[Humour and satire — "Der Kokh-lefl": antisemitism / Sunday rest.]
The Endek [National Democrat] editor had a terrible night. He dreamt a terrible dream:
It was Saturday morning, all the shops were closed. Jews in silk kapotes, with coloured Turkish pocket-handkerchiefs in their hands, were walking about on broad Third of May Street in the "Rozwój" bazaar, trying the locks of the shops. Young Żydki hide in the gentile courtyards and keep watch whether anyone is being let in "round the back". If they catch a gentile butcher letting a gentile woman out through the back door, they immediately run to inform, and a report is drawn up.
Jewish gendarmes with a gendarmerie rotmistrz (captain) circle the "Rozwój" market and chase everyone off the market.
On the pavement of Dekerta Street, where the town synagogue stands, the Christians are chased off, because a divine service is taking place in the synagogue, and therefore no Christian may be found anywhere in the vicinity.
The Polish shops are more often shut than open. Every Monday and Thursday they (the Żydzi) have holidays: here the birthday of a rabbinical-court beadle, there the shloshim of a grave-measuring woman, today fast days, a yoma de-pagra [day off], and just plain "świętas".
— — — — — — — —
Starting awake from this terrible dream, he (the Endek editor) was drenched in cold sweat and panting. He immediately got out of bed, grabbed his pen and wrote a fiery article:
"Compulsory Sabbath Rest in the Polish Republic".
Poor "Rozwójnik", in your struggle for "honesty" and "tolerance" may you find consolation.
Honig Foygl [Honey Bird].

The Night of Vigil in the Będzin Kehilla

[Będzin — Kehilla.]
[Page 7 — "Zaglembier Tsaytung", No. 52 — "What's New in Zagłębie?" — Friday, 24 Kislev 5693 / 23 December 1932 — Będzin]
Officials' pensions cut. — A threat from the rabbinate. — Pensions for the new shochtim struck out. — A supplementary budget to finish the mikveh. — Subsidies struck out.
The old kehilla council has risen again, "resurrection of the dead", and come into the kehilla to approve the new budget.
And nothing has changed. The same half-asleep council, the same gallery, the same debates and the same — abuse...
In this respect there was a slight change this year. It was not the council members who fought among themselves, but only the board members (dozór) Rinski (Agudah) and Liwer (Zionist).
The fight was often passionate; it went beyond the bounds of the budget, and each "honoured" the other with "parliamentary" expressions, especially at the moment when Mr. Rinski demanded that Mr. Liwer "prove to him that he puts on tefillin"...
—
The first budget session took place on Thursday under the chairmanship of the President, Mr. Jakub Gutman (יאקוב גוטמאן).
Before the agenda, board member Mr. Liwer takes the floor and turns to the council with a motion that, since not a single item of the old budget was carried out by the administration, the council should, as a protest, not approve this year's budget.
The council majority is against the motion, and they proceed to the budget.
The first item is: pensions for the rabbi and members of the rabbinate. The administration cut the pensions of the moreh hora'ah (rabbinic judges) by 15 percent, and the rabbi's pension — by 10 percent.
Board member Rinski delivers the budget "exposé" on behalf of the administration. The exposé is an optimistic one. The sad situation of the gmina is — he says — due only to the prevailing crisis, which has led to the pensions of the gmina officials being cut by 15 percent. But since the rabbi himself had earlier proposed to cut his pension by 10 percent, the administration accepted this as a fine gesture and agreed to the rabbi's proposal.
Board member Mr. Liwer makes a longer speech, in which he points out that the catastrophic situation in the gmina was brought about by the administration's bad management. The gmina — he says — is bankrupt both morally and materially. Mr. Liwer also criticises the rabbi's "gesture". If the rabbi — he says — had intended [?] the "gesture", why did he go to the homes of some of the kehilla representatives and ask them that his pension not be reduced? I therefore propose that the system of reduction be proportional to the size of the pension.
Liwer's motion fails, and the administration's proposal is adopted.
On the pensions of the office officials, the parnas Mr. Józef Szwajcer proposes that, since the officials have no side income, their pensions be cut by 10 per cent. The motion, which is also supported by board member Mr. Goldsztajn, fails, and it is adopted, per the administration, to cut by 15 percent.
A good deal of "mouse-squeaking" floats up during the item pension for a cantor. Here Mr. Liwer again criticises the gmina's management, reporting that the cantor Mr. Żupowicz [?] obtained a court judgment (wyrok) for 11 thousand zl.
By a majority of votes the item is struck out. With the amendment of the parnas Mr. G. Rechnic, to increase(!) the sum from 500 to 1000 zl. for repair purposes in the synagogue.
A bitter fight played out between Messrs. Liwer and Rinski over the item: pensions for the new young shochtim, for whom the administration had "for the time being" set 2,400 zl. a year.
The first to speak on the question is the parnas Mr. Rechnic, who comes out against the pensions for the new shochtim for the following reasons: 1) to take on a shochet a competition must be published; 2) the slaughtering income has diminished considerably. The 3 old shochtim are enough; if that is too few, one of the dayanim (mo"tz) should be present at the slaughtering; and 3) the gmina need not pay pensions to apprentice lads who want to qualify in the slaughterhouse.
The motion is supported by Mr. Liwer and others. Against it speaks Mr. Rinski, who appeals to the council with the verse "and thou shalt fear thy God": remember — he cries out — what you are about to do; a holy war will flare up in the town; the "Va'ad ha-Kashrut", around which 60 houses of prayer are grouped, will come out with a declaration of war.
The "arguments" have little influence, and by a majority of votes Mr. Rechnic's motion to strike out the pensions for the new young shochtim is adopted. Instead the pension of R' Yisrael Moshe, shochet u-bodek, is restored as before, i.e. 6.623 zl. a year, so that he can give the young shochtim something out of the pension.
With this the session closes at 3:30 a.m.
—
The continuation took place on Sunday. The first "bomb" that "went off" was the motion of R' Mendel Rozenzaft, who asks the council to allocate a sum of 30 thousand zl. to finish the mikveh.
This point too dragged up a bit of "mud" around what is called — "kehilla activity", and Mr. Liwer's motion is adopted to make a special supplementary budget, with the income monies of this supplementary budget to be in the hands of several respected citizens.
Then the subsidies were dealt with "in one breath" at the level the administration had set.
Among the subsidies, a new "important" item has also been added in this year's budget, namely the Va'ad ha-Kashrut (misprinted "ha-Chashrut"; jokers call it the "Va'ad ha-Shkarut", the committee of lies...), for which 200 zl. was set. (The administration was for 1,200 zl.
Finally it should also be added that the members of the rabbinate and the new young shochtim have sent letters to the council in which they threaten "consequences" and "other steps" if the council commits any injustice against them regarding the pensions.

Just have your trade books stamped through the “ALFA” bureau

Advance payments (zaliczki) on turnover tax for the year 1933 will be smaller.
In connection with the fact that from the New Year onward the turnover tax on retail trade and on handicrafts will become much smaller, the merchants are mistaken about the advance payments.
The merchants think, namely, that the new advance payments for 1933 will be based on the assessment of turnover tax for 1932, as is done every year, and that one will have to pay in 80 percent of the turnover to be assessed for 1932, payable in 4 instalments.
Fortunately, this will not be so.
Paragraph 82 of the Finance Minister's implementing regulations to the turnover-tax law explains clearly and plainly how this must be done. This paragraph states, namely, that from now on the turnover tax given according to the turnover assessed in the last tax assessment will become smaller every year, but the tax rate (stawka) is to be calculated according to the new current year in which the advance payments are paid.
So, we will explain this with an example: in the present year a textile (manufaktura) merchant had his turnover (obrót) assessed at 100 thousand zł., and he therefore had to pay 2,500 zł. tax; on that basis he had to pay advance payments of 500 zł. every quarter in 1932. On 15 April 1933 the turnover will again be assessed at 100 thousand zł., and the turnover tax for 1932 will again amount to 1,500 zł. But the advance-payment notices will now be sent out for only 250 zł. every quarter of a year.
Craftsmen who hold craftsman's cards will also receive smaller advance payments in 1933.
It goes without saying that the turnover can be assessed as the office in each town sees fit.
Those who keep simplified bookkeeping, or the big merchants who keep books, will be assessed only as much as the bookkeeping shows, and they will pay a much smaller turnover rate (stawka obrotowa).

(A reply to the “Linat ha-Holim” concerning the activity of our society “Bikur Holim” in Old Sosnowiec.)
Our institution was created because the “Linat ha-Holim” did not provide the proper help (above all with medical equipment) to the great poor population living in Old Sosnowiec.
Thanks to the founding of “Bikur Holim” the poor sick receive all the necessary means of help, such as doctors, medicines, equipment and the like. At our expense the most difficult operations are performed in the Jewish hospital; in this field we can say with pride that through our help dozens of souls have been saved from death.
Such facts can be confirmed by the esteemed feldsher Mr. Teichner [?], who knows that at three o'clock at night we called out Dr. Jankowski for an operation, and thanks to that the Jew was kept alive.
It is possible that the particulars of the great number of facts may not find favour with the gentlemen of the “great” “Linat ha-Holim” with its “ramified” administrative apparatus; incidentally, that makes no great difference to us. We only intend to make public that when we turned to these gentlemen to lend us collection boxes (tarbes) for our badge sale, they refused us with the excuse that “the public will be misled”. Our argument that the press had written about it, and that the badge too bears the name of “Bikur Holim”, did not help — they nevertheless did not lend the boxes, for one must after all preserve the tsarist [?] traditions that the sister-institution “Bikur Holim” is treyf; and what is more, the holy law of “Linat ha-Holim” lays down that it is forbidden to lend a piece of equipment to a sick person whose fate is to live in Old Sosnowiec... This despite the fact that we too are partners in the equipment of “Linat ha-Holim”, since we too pay dues [?] to the Sosnowiec gmina, which bought the equipment...
As to the accusation that we take money throughout the whole town, we declare that this is a base lie. On the other hand it is a fact that the “Linat ha-Holim” takes money throughout the whole town, collects in Old Sosnowiec too, even at weddings [?], and supports only individual “kosher” members — and of course not at all those from Old Sosnowiec...
If the gentlemen of the “Linat ha-Holim” were honest communal workers and intent on helping the poor sick, they ought to be grateful to us and appreciate our great, honest and humanitarian deeds; but instead of gratitude they have the audacity to insult us, and in particular our tireless and esteemed chairman Mr. Reuven Czapnik [?], who accomplishes so much for our society.
This is what we wished to make clear, and we will conduct no further polemic with these gentlemen. Respectfully,

Propaganda Meeting for the Benefit of the Gemilut Chesed Fund in Dąbrowa

[Dąbrowa — Community and Mutual Aid.] In the premises of "TUR" in Dąbrowa a propaganda meeting took place, organized by the board of the Gemilut Chesed [interest-free loan] fund in Dąbrowa.
Taking part in the meeting were the local rabbi; representatives of the same kind of funds from Będzin in the persons of Messrs. Rubinlicht and Bożykowski; from Sosnowiec — Mr. L. Zendel; kehilla board members, Jewish city councillors and a large public.
The meeting is opened by the chairman of the G[emilut] Ch[esed] fund, Mr. Rubinsztejn, and after the short introduction and the report of Mr. Winer, Messrs. Rubinlicht, Zendel, Wygodzki and Bożykowski speak, pointing out the important role that the self-help funds play at the present moment, when the Jewish community is so broken and impoverished. The speakers also level sharp reproaches at the Jewish population of Dąbrowa, which has been so indifferent to the institution, which today counts no more than 50 members...
A discussion develops over the reproaches, in which Messrs. Winer, Councillor Rechnic, Szpilberg, Sztajnberg, Chairman Najfeld and Councillor Szczęgowski take part; they declare that the blame for the fund not having developed falls on the board up to now, which ran its activity within the framework of a "shtibl" [small prayer house] and did not want to admit to the work anyone who was not a member of that shtibl fraternity.
The board members, Messrs. Złotnik, Brandes, Balicki and others, reject the accusation and point out that the board turned many times to the Jewish public for support, and their voice always remained like a voice crying in the wilderness.
Tempers flare, chaos reigns in the hall and it looks like an election rally...
After the closing speeches of the local rabbi, the dozór [kehilla board] member Granitman and Zendel, the following resolution is put to the vote at the proposal of Editor Lewkowicz:
"Having heard the speeches at the propaganda meeting, which took place on Monday the 26th inst. in the premises of 'TUR' with the participation of several hundred people, [the meeting] resolves to carry out during this month a recruitment campaign that will raise the G.Ch. fund to its proper level, and calls on the Jewish population of Dąbrowa to join the G.Ch. fund as members."
The resolution is adopted unanimously with Mr. Zendel's amendment that a committee be formed on the spot to carry out the recruitment campaign.
The committee so formed includes representatives of all strata of the Jewish population of Dąbrowa.
The exact text of the Finance Ministry's circular on reliefs in purchasing [trade] patents for the year 1933

[Economy — taxes.] The Finance Ministry has issued circular G. L. D. P. 53531/4/32 of the 14th of this month, under which commercial enterprises of the 2nd and 3rd category may be run — without individual applications — on the basis of a trade patent [trade licence certificate, świadectwo przemysłowe] of category 3 instead of 2, if their turnover in 1931 did not exceed 30 thousand zł., and on a category 4 instead of the 3rd, if the turnover did not exceed 10 thousand zł.
Without submitting applications, gastronomic establishments may also be run on the basis of the 3rd category instead of the 2nd, if their turnover in 1931 was not higher than 20 thousand zł.
Restaurants, confectioneries [cukiernie], cafés [kawiarnie], beer-houses and dairy bars [mleczarnie] may be run on the basis of a 3rd category, if domestic beverages are sold in the establishment and if the number of employees does not exceed 10 persons.
Bookshops with a side sale of writing materials may be run on the basis of a 3rd category, if their turnover in 1931 did not exceed the sum of 30 thousand zł.
On the basis of submitted applications, the Treasury Chambers [izby skarbowe] may entirely exempt from purchasing patents those enterprises whose turnover in 1931 amounted to no more than 2000 zł. The same also applies to holders of category 5 patents.
Pharmaceutical stores [składy apteczne] may purchase a 3rd category instead of a second, if their turnover in 1931 amounted to no more than 30 thousand zł.
The applications must be submitted to the tax office [urząd skarbowy]. The deadline for submitting the applications already ends on 31 December. In the case of new enterprises, the applications must be submitted before opening the business. The taxpayer must receive the reply to the application by 1 March. In case the Treasury Chamber refuses, the decision cannot be appealed. At the same time the Finance Ministry draws the Treasury Chambers' attention to treating the proposals of the tax offices critically.
The Finance Ministry also permits the side sale of tobacco products to be carried on without a patent in bookshops and in other commercial enterprises, if the sale takes place in the same premises.

On Guard Against a Catastrophe

[Opinion — Zagłębie, interest-free loan funds.]
(XVI. For the propaganda month for the gemilut-chesed funds in Zagłębie.)
F. Szpigelman.
The central office of the gemilut-chesed (interest-free loan) funds in Poland has proclaimed the present month a month of propaganda throughout the whole country.
Who and what the g"ch funds in the country are, what role they play and once played in our homely little world, in the Jewish milieu [?], every one of us knows; we know very well to what extent they did or did not perform, to what extent they brought benefit here or there. We know that many, very many errors, and cardinal errors, were quite often made. More than once we dealt with the question, and after a precise elucidation and argument we stated our opinion and at the same time pointed out the harmful ways, the catastrophic future for this or that local fund; but people preened themselves [?] and did not want to reckon with anyone or anything, so that the managers rose to the rank of autocrats, to the phase of dictators. Because of various similar defects of not reckoning with the public, the institutions sank to a second-rate level, people began to reckon less and less with the institutions, and the prestige vanished and the lustre faded of this institution, useful in all times.
For us, however, the institutions were too holy, too dear and beloved for us to reckon with anybody's caprice, and already before the founding, before the establishment of the institutions here in Zagłębie, we said that in creating them, in realizing them, it must be done on a broad scale. The gesture must be European, modern, and around them must concentrate the finest of Jewry, the best of society, and responsible for their deeds must be the whole community, the broad circles of Jewish society. We were against making little cliques for individuals out of it. More than once we pointed out that the institutions must serve the whole people, and therefore representatives of all strata of the population must concentrate around them; in our opinion, therefore, the g"ch funds must be non-partisan; they must serve the single aim: to help everyone who needs their support.
We believe that the honest people, devoted heart and soul, who led the institutions, have by now acquired the proper practice, and I have no wish to repeat the disharmony and the vexing and painful deeds that happened when they happened, because of which the prestige fell and confidence vanished.
Today a propaganda month has been proclaimed for the said institutions throughout the country. We know very well that nowadays it is very, very hard to persuade another to support this or that undertaking and to help it. For we know how hard it is in the prevailing critical time to earn a livelihood. Who even talks about sparing a gulden [one złoty], which one could afford to put aside for charity — every one of us knows how hard that is to fulfil. But one must not take the matter of existence too tragically, one must not ponder it too much, not delve too deeply into it, because common sense plays a scant role here; with logic and calculation one will achieve little here. And so we always push our way through; one can say that we often live by miracles, beyond nature. It often happens that one sees palpably that the Jewish people in this or that country is already right at the brink of destruction, at the edge of the sea, with no other way out than destruction — and suddenly, we know not whence or where from, some new horizons appear, fresh stars, which bring in new sources of life, a fresh stream of life.
More than once we have had occasion to see this for ourselves; evidently we really do belong to that wondrous people which cannot vanish, which cannot be wiped off the globe. Be that as it may, and in whatever manner they may wish to annihilate us, we push our way through. With sweat and blood we fight for today and for tomorrow, which come to us unnaturally hard, but we nonetheless bore our way through to existence.
Yes, we live and hope. We hope and live beyond natural possibilities, beyond human reason, and therefore we must also now reckon that with all our strength, with all our most impossible possibilities, we must set about carrying out successfully the propaganda month for the g"ch funds.
What the g"ch funds are there is no need to tell anyone. Everyone knows that the institution was created, and its task everywhere and always is not to let fall into the abyss the one who trades, those who earn somehow or other; when someone is barely holding on from collapsing, the task of the g"ch funds is to keep him on his feet and help restore his existence to health with a little capital. Gemilut chesed has always been among Jews one of the greatest mitzvot, all the more so now, when credit is not given and capital has become such a great rarity. With a loan at the present moment one keeps a person alive, and with it he sustains, somehow, his hard and bitter struggle for existence.
Zagłębie, when it wants, can give, and in truth it can do so only because it has understanding for it; attitude plays a great role here, and therefore we hold that Zagłębie and Upper Silesia will certainly fulfil their duty and prove that they can support others even at a moment when they themselves have become impoverished.
It does not matter — one may speak the truth to one's face: the best-situated corner in Poland is on the road to impoverishment, our population grows poorer from day to day, and yet we shall not lose heart. The Zagłębie Jew is just like that: as long as he has, he shares with others. We here cannot let anyone fall, and therefore we should show the central office in Warsaw that we have understanding and regard for this holy and useful popular work.
Zagłębie will certainly show its love, respect and devotion to the holy ideal; therefore we shall continue to demand responsibility and properly fruitful work, which should help rescue the middle class in the country, which has almost already lost the ground from under its feet.
And because the times are bad, because the situation of the community is incomprehensibly critical, therefore, if one wants to accomplish something and create the necessary material support, one is obliged to approach the campaign with a definite plan, which should bring substantial help, which the g"ch funds need so badly in order to be able to begin working with fresh money and with intensive forces.
No one wants to doubt that the institution is [not] necessary to the Jewish community simply like life itself, but each of us also wants the assurance that the management will be exemplary and useful, one that will support all who need support, even on the smallest scale, at a minimum.
People have begun to look upon institutions in general as a superfluous object one can do without, and that only because Jewish society lost its confidence in its institutions, seeing that they had been turned into toys and party shops.
True, this cannot yet be said of the g"ch funds; but one forgets in a single week that the everyday Jew, the Jew who has little in mind of social problems, cannot sort things out, does not find his bearings and does not feel the need to carry out the proper analysis — and so, for these people, for this category of Jews, one is obliged to explain the matter of what a gemilut-chesed fund is.
Zagłębie must help pour a fresh stream of vital spirit into the g"ch funds, so that they may have the possibility of continuing the hard, fruitful social work they have begun for the benefit of the one who needs the loan, which can set him on his feet; therefore we shall continue to demand a mutual, satisfactory relationship.
We find ourselves in a very hard economic situation. The situation is catastrophic, almost unavoidable; therefore we must be on the watch and guard our interests, and if we fulfil this, we shall know that we have done what our conscience demands of us, so that thereby we shall have fulfilled a satisfying duty which every one of us is obliged to pay; but he has for it the satisfaction of knowing that by fulfilling this human duty he has brought benefit to the community, to the broad strata of the Jewish population.

Getting Ready for Sylvester (New Year's Eve)...

[Feuilleton — New Year's Eve.]
In short, gentlemen, no worrying... Throw out of your heads all your worries about taxes, debts, protested bills, boycott and other plagues, and get ready to welcome the holiday...
I see, gentlemen, that you are staring at me with a pair of astonished eyes, as if to say: what kind of holiday is this, out of the blue? Till Passover, as is well established („kima lan“), we still have 4 months; we have only just said the blessing over the Hanukkah candles, and many a shiver we will yet catch from the terrible frosts and blizzards („zavierukhes“, Polish zawierucha) that the cruel Winter-King will grant us with his full hand — so what holiday are we talking about here?
I tell you, gentlemen, that a holiday is coming all the same, and what a holiday! With dances and song and with champagne — for those whom God helps — and with beer and soda water — for those whom God does not help; but celebrate it everyone will, from small to great, from poor to rich; all are waiting impatiently for its arrival.
I see, gentlemen, that you have already guessed whom I mean: indeed, that dear[?] holiday whose name is Sylvester...
To all the holidays
that are dear to us,
there has now been added
a holiday, a new one,
a „Jewish“ holiday
that is called Sylvester:
one dances and carouses,
one presses ever closer,
to the sounds of the jazz band,
to the noise of the orchestra...
Say what you like, gentlemen, I hold that the Jews are doing well to have naturalised „Sylvester“ and to celebrate it with splendour, no worse than the nations of the world. What of it? Why shouldn't Jews rejoice as is fitting? Do we sigh too little all year round? Must we be candidates only for shedding tears?...
And weeping, indeed —
do we weep too little, then?
Come now, just take and count:
one weeps on Yom Kippur
for a good verdict („kvitl“),
one weeps at Eikhah, small and great,
one weeps at the Kinot,
one weeps at Selichot,
one groans whole days and nights...
So to laugh
is one not allowed a little?
Eh... let it be... it's not bad at all...
For, let us not fool ourselves, we know well what happiness we can expect from the new year. It will bluff us, sweet-talk us, like its older colleague, and promise us good tidings, salvation and consolation — and afterwards it will all turn out to be a flop, yesterday's day!...
So let us at least grab in grand style[?] a few good merry hours... That will be just like a find, because what you don't grab, you don't have — so say the Zaglembie merchants and manufacturers when they stand on the eve of bankruptcy...
Grabbing — that has today become a programme for all states and nations and even for parties: Japan wants to grab China, the German wants to grab the „Corridor“, Hitler wants to grab power, Lithuania wants to grab Vilna, the „Agudah“ wants to grab the kehillot.
And he who does not grab — he indeed has nothing...
Therefore let us too grab a bit of pleasure and make ourselves merry and jolly, and indeed take that genuine little drop of liquor, until... until we forget ourselves... To forget — that is nowadays the most precious prescription, which we need more than anything... To forget that there is such a creature in the world called the bailiff, who has a mighty longing for your bit of household furniture; to forget — that you have a wife and grown-up daughters who have and need and want...; to forget that you have a son at the university and they want[?] to make a cripple of him by force.
To forget that you are hated because you made a bad choice and picked yourself a father named Shmuel or Khatskl and not Jan or Wojtek...
A little bit of opium, gentlemen,
is healthy for us now,
we must forget our troubles,
forget — we are going under...
forget the dark shadows
that frighten with hatred and with shame,
forget that we are Jews,
a people without a home, without a land...
As you see, gentlemen, „memory“ is not always a virtue. There are such times for people when it is better and healthier to lose one's memory... when one can forget oneself.
Therefore, gentlemen, prepare in good time the real masks. Whatever else, in masks there is no shortage among us... Who can disguise himself so well that he is not recognised, as we Jews can? Who has so many clowns and comedians and spiritual acrobats as we Jews?...
Do you know the Jewish manufacturer X? In his factory you won't find a Jewish worker for love or money. In his office Germans and Poles work, and Jews — barely a handful. His daughter attends a Christian boarding school. What more do you need? Even for a mistress („kokhanke“, Polish kochanka) he picked himself a gentile. Nevertheless he wears the mask of a pious Jew and goes to pray precisely in a shtibl...
I know someone, a dyed-in-the-wool heretic, who speaks „against the Lord and against His anointed“ — and when Rosh Hashanah comes, you find him in the synagogue, wrapped in his tallit over his head and swaying with relish over the makhzor...
Well, would you say that is a bad clown?...
And what about our communal workers and „dozor“ (community board) members, may they be healthy, who play the role of providers for the people and „benefactors“ and have their own interests in mind besides? Never mind, we have no need to be ashamed of them either..

Emigration (Special for the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" — Eng. Uri Gliklich)

[Essay — Emigration and Zionism.] Emigration.
Special for the "Zaglembier Tsaytung".
By Eng. Uri Gliklich.

The word "emigration" has always been "popular" among the Jewish masses, among Jewish youth. Today, however, it is — the only ideal, the one and only redeemer.

Never before has the emigration question been so burning as today, because never before have poverty and despair been so terrible, so frightful; because never before has want, Jewish want, looked so straight and so mercilessly into our eyes as now.

Across the larger cities of Poland one often sees the roving wagons of the Jewish relief committees, which stop at the corners of various streets and hand out a glass of tea and a piece of bread free of charge. Since the pieces of bread are small, people have hit upon a trick: they run after the cart to the next street corner and — ask once again..!

Such sad pictures are seen not only in Poland, but also in various regions of Romania, of Lithuania, of Carpathian Ruthenia, etc. The "Central-Verein" of German citizens of the Mosaic faith has issued an appeal, from which it is plainly evident that want has ceased to be a specific "monopoly" of Eastern Jewry; it has also penetrated the European ghetto walls.

The sources of livelihood are being blocked more and more with every passing day, the possibilities of existence undermined.

About our middle class (Mittelstand) a characteristic saying goes around: that it is "a class without means" (a Stand ohne Mittel), because not only does the tax press squeeze out all its living juices, not only does the government not even consider where it is to draw its income from — on the contrary, it pulls the ground out from under its feet and does everything to ruin it.

Yes, the "Mah-Yafit" Jewlets try to persuade us that this is not a purely Jewish phenomenon, but nobody takes their words seriously: everyone sees that Jewish livelihoods are being taken away without a why or a wherefore. What wonder, then, that the word "emigration" has become a spell, an incantation for millions of Jews!!

At the same time America has almost completely closed its gates. The same with South Africa, and the other overseas countries follow the same example. About Europe there is, after all, nothing to say: even France, which until not long ago was hospitable, has already learned the wisdom of tightening entry.

Four years ago Y. Gruenbaum had the courage to say that in Poland there is a surplus million. Now that figure of "surplus" is already too small — it would be more correct to speak of a million and a half. In all of Eastern Europe there are probably about three million "surplus" Jews. "Surplus" not only now, during the world crisis. For the non-Jewish world the crisis will pass: people will raise their heads anew and stand back on their feet. But the twisted, broken Jewish "economies" will no longer recover, just as an uprooted tree will no longer blossom, even though the storm has long since passed.

Everyone knows this. And the Jews have known it for a long time; and that is why Zionism exists in the world. One must finally put an end to the so-called "scientific chatter" that Zionism never set itself the aim of saving the Jewish people from want and hunger. Precisely that aim is the one it set itself. Never has any Jew imagined that the final goal of the Redemption would be the creation of a paradise in Eretz Israel for a few minyanim of Jews, while the great people would go on starving and languishing in Europe and knocking at the doors of America. If any Jew really believed that w i t h t h a t the whole Zionist élan would end, he would turn away and say: such a "redemption" I do not want.

Not a plaything, not a "trinket" for the select few, but a serious and a great and an all-embracing "purpose".

The "scientific character" of the above-mentioned chatter was very simple. There are about 16 million Jews in the world, and Eretz Israel cannot take them all in.

But the economic, the "rescuing" task of Zionism does not consist in evacuating all Jews from the Diaspora. Even regarding Poland nobody has said that all three million are economically "surplus". There is a certain percentage of the Jewish admixture which the Diaspora can indeed sustain, which the Diaspora can economically absorb without upheavals. But whatever exceeds that percentage must be evacuated — otherwise a chronic death-agony threatens it, all the worse because it may not lead so quickly to extinction. Exactly how many such "surplus" people there are in each country — I do not know.

One thing is clear: there are countries where the percentage of the "surplus" is larger, and there are countries where the percentage of the "surplus" is smaller. For example — Poland, Germany, Tunis and Morocco.

The exact figure will become clear in practice: if in our "National Home" the gates are really open, both in the political and in the economic sense, then all those for whom there is no economic place in the Diaspora will gradually go there. On the basis of the examples of peoples with a large diaspora (for instance the Irish) one can try to estimate: there are 4 million economically "surplus" Jews in the world. Their aliyah to Eretz Israel would normalise the situation of those remaining; just as, if a third were taken out of a hall packed with an audience, the remaining two thirds could move about comfortably and have air to breathe.

Four million emigrants to Eretz Israel is not a fantastic task. Without Transjordan, without cultivation, without ports and roads, without connection to the hinterland, nearly a million people live in Eretz Israel today! And what will there be with corresponding development?

That is the economic side of today's Zionist task — to make Eretz Israel capable of absorbing millions of Jewish emigrants. All our political demands spring from this very awareness. A Jewish majority in Eretz Israel is not yet the final goal of Zionism; that majority will come when the first three-quarters of a million have entered the country, but that is only the first step; full redemption will only then become the task and the concern of the Jewish state.

Thus, and only thus, must the Zionist problem be posed today.

The Instalment Trade Will Have to Go Under

[Economy — instalment trade and legislation.]
As is known, on 1 January 1933 the new Code of Civil Procedure comes into force. Under this code, it will not be possible to proceed against the salary of an official or a worker for a debt if the monthly wage is not higher than 100 zł. This point of the new code has caused an uproar among all the persons engaged in trade on instalments ["rates", Polish raty].
It is pointed out that because of this article of the new code the instalment trade will have to go under, since the greater part of the customers of this trade are recruited chiefly from workers, caretakers [stróże] and other small employees whose salaries do not exceed 100 zł. a month.
Until now, if a merchant had sold on instalments and the instalments were not paid, he had the possibility of attaching one fifth of the salary, and in this way he got his money. Under the new code, however, this will no longer be possible.
